samples.summary: Design doc now asserts a blanket "a dry run never reaches the network" contract, but six sibling read commands outside the diff still fetch under --dry-run
samples.evidence: The change is accompanied by docs/design/cli.md:824-827 ("Reads honour the flag too … A dry run never reaches the network, so it burns no rate limit and emits no access log even when the command is harmless"), and the new test header repeats it. That universal claim is false for the read commands the diff did not touch, all of which call the client with no `opts.dryRun` guard: packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:40 (`slides list`), slides.ts:81 (`slides get`), packages/cli/src/commands/notes.ts:35 (`notes list`), notes.ts:76 (`notes get`), packages/cli/src/commands/files.ts:85 (`files list`), files.ts:105 (`files get`), and packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:39 (`sheets export`, which issues GET /cells before writing the file). An agent that reads the new doc sentence and pre-flights `slides list --dry-run` or `sheets export … --dry-run` still hits the API — and `sheets export` additionally writes the output file. Fix belongs either on those call sites or on the new doc wording (narrow it to the four commands actually changed).

samples.summary: New dry-run branches in `docs get` and `tabs list` sit outside the command's try/catch, unlike every other dry-run site in the CLI
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:125-128 and packages/cli/src/commands/tabs.ts:14-17 call `getConfig(opts)`/`printDryRun` before the `try {`. Every pre-existing dry-run site keeps the call inside the try so a throw becomes the documented `{ error: { code, message } }` envelope with exit 1 (e.g. docs.ts:106-111, slides.ts:59-66, files.ts:57-61); the `docs list` branch added in this same diff (docs.ts:78-83) does it correctly. `resolveConfig` currently swallows its own failures and `runCli` (packages/cli/src/cli.ts:75-91) is a last-resort catch, so the observable behaviour is unchanged today — but the two new sites are inconsistent with the convention the rest of the file relies on.

verdict.reason: All cited evidence checks out against the repository. docs/design/cli.md:824-827 does contain the unconditional sentence "A dry run never reaches the network, so it burns no rate limit and emits no access log even when the command is harmless." --dry-run is a GLOBAL option declared once at packages/cli/src/commands/root.ts:75 and surfaced to every subcommand via optsWithGlobals (root.ts:24-27), so the contract applies repo-wide. The named sibling read commands genuinely lack any dryRun branch and call the HTTP client unconditionally: slides.ts:40 (listDocuments), slides.ts:81 (getDocument), notes.ts:35, notes.ts:76, files.ts:85, files.ts:105. sheets-export.ts:39 issues getCells and sheets-export.ts:51 then writeFileSync's the output file, so `sheets export --dry-run` both hits the API and creates/overwrites a local file. These sit alongside guarded siblings in the very same files (slides.ts:60/94/112/141/197, notes.ts:55/89/107/135/195, files.ts:58/118/136, docs.ts:78-83), confirming the inconsistency rather than an intentional per-command opt-out reachable through some other guard. No upstream interceptor for opts.dryRun exists — grep for dryRun across packages/cli/src/commands shows only per-action branches. This is in the blast-radius lane: an invariant newly asserted for the shared --dry-run flag with reachable entry points that bypass it, one of which additionally writes to disk; impact is major (a guard/contract with reachable bypasses left inconsistent), and it is real, not merely a diff-internal logic question.
